newsitem.title: DENMARK: Unidanmark seeks mortgage bond rating. [CORRECTED 15:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Unidanmark seeks mortgage bond rating. [CORRECTED 15:05 GMT]

text.p: Danish banking group Unidanmark said on Monday that its Unikredit mortgage unit planned to seek a Moody's rating for its mortgage-backed bonds in the hope of attracting more overseas investors.

"I believe that it will make (Danish mortgage bonds) more visible overseas and we shall perhaps see a larger flow of mortgage-backed paper across borders," deputy-director Claus K. Moeller told Reuters.
Unidanmark's main rivals Den Danske Bank and Nykredit last week became the first Danish issuers to be graded by U.S. ratings agency Moody's on their mortgage-backed bonds.

Nykredit, Denmark's largest mortgage lender and allied with third-biggest bank BG Bank, won an Aa3 Moody's rating on its Capital Centre 3 series of mortgage-bonds, representing some 55 percent of the company's mortgage paper and slated to grow.
Den Danske Bank, Denmark's biggest bank, won an Aa2 (corrects from Aa3) rating covering all of its mortgage-backed bonds.
Some 910 billion crowns in mortgage-backed bonds were outstanding on July 31, accounting for 53 percent of all bonds on the Copenhagen exchange.
Unibank expects its rating within the next few months.
